action_summary: Closes the last link that 'experience each action once' leaves open, and states the bottleneck it exposes. One success leaves 4 distinct behaviours alive (16 of 56 hypotheses) on every real action measured, because a success is a point in the domain while applicability is its boundary. On ten real actions and 19 coordinates, one REFUSAL per coordinate -- not a try -- identifies the precondition 10/10 (one distinct behaviour, equal to the true one), where the previous round's 160 state interventions identified 0/10 with best accuracy 1.0. The refusal is a declaration, not a hint: its message is injective over the violated coordinate and invariant under a different distractor, 10/10 each, measured without reading English. Refusals change no object (36/38 byte-identical, the 2 exceptions wrote only patch's own .rej), so the boundary costs zero effect. Three published checks were measured not to mean their fact: tar -tzf accepts a gzip of garbage (exit 0), git stash list exits 0 on an empty list, and patch writes a .rej before refusing. Result: the operator has two halves -- effect from a success, precondition from a refusal -- and the schedule is 1 success + k refusals, 48 executions, 0.6 s, 0 model calls, 0 parameters.
